operations_plan.summary: Establish the common center axis, original flower-interface depth, and a parameterized regular hexagonal master profile for the replacement torque interface.

steps.description: Temporarily isolate the separate center insert from the sprocket carrier. Recover the common rotational axis from the insert pilot cylinder and internal spline bore, cross-checking it against the carrier socket pilot cylinder. Use this axis as the center and normal of every replacement-profile sketch so the internal spline, hexagonal interface, and sprocket pitch circle remain concentric.

Measure the axial start plane, end plane, and depth of the existing flower-shaped engagement from the planar flange lands and the matching carrier socket transitions. Record these as interface_start_z and interface_depth. The hexagonal replacement must occupy exactly this axial interval; do not extend it through the preserved circular rear boss, internal spline, or unrelated hub shoulders.

Create a master sketch on the planar face at interface_start_z, normal to the recovered center axis. Project the existing flower-profile boundary and relevant surrounding hub limits into the sketch as construction geometry. Draw a fully constrained regular six-sided polygon centered on the common axis. The requested hexagon size is unresolved; define it parametrically as hex_insert_across_flats and, unless a design value is supplied, set it to the largest across-flats value that keeps the insert hexagon within the minimum radial envelope of the existing flower profile and maintains the existing minimum carrier wall thickness. The requested orientation is also unresolved; use the existing +Y centerline or corresponding flower-lobe datum as the provisional angular datum, placing one hexagon vertex on that line. Keep the orientation parameter editable.

Create a second, concentric hexagonal profile for the carrier socket by offsetting the master insert hexagon outward by a parameter named hex_radial_clearance. Derive the provisional clearance from the existing radial clearance between the flower flange and mating socket where measurable; otherwise leave it as an unresolved manufacturing parameter requiring fit specification. Constrain both hexagons to the same angular datum so their six planar torque faces are parallel.

operations_plan.summary: Replace the flower-shaped mating socket in the annular carrier with a concentric hexagonal socket while preserving the surrounding spider, annular shoulder, and circular pilot geometry.

steps.description: Suppress or remove the original repeated flower-socket construction if feature history is available. In a direct-modeling workflow, delete and heal the lobed conical and cylindrical socket faces, then restore material over only the recorded interface_depth to form an uncut carrier blank. Bound the repair by the existing annular shoulder and surrounding center-carrier material. Do not alter the continuous circular pilot wall, outer annular shoulder, radial ribs, aperture boundaries, or spider face contours.

Use the offset carrier-hex profile to make a pocket or Boolean cut into solid 1 from interface_start_z through exactly interface_depth. Terminate the cut on the original socket end plane rather than cutting through the complete hub. The resulting socket must have six planar axial walls, remain concentric with face 669, and retain sufficient material between its vertices and the adjoining spider roots.

Recreate the socket entry transition around the new hexagonal opening. Apply a uniform lead-in chamfer to the six entry edges using the existing flower-socket chamfer depth and angle as reference. At the six internal corners, use only the minimum manufacturing radius required by the intended process; keep this radius smaller than hex_radial_clearance so it does not interfere with the insert vertices. Preserve the original annular axial shoulder represented by face 667 and the circular lead-in and pilot represented by faces 668 and 669 wherever they lie outside the replaced interface.

operations_plan.summary: Rebuild the separate insert's external flower-shaped drive flange as the matching regular hexagonal male profile without changing the internal spline or preserved circular boss and pilot.

steps.description: Suppress the original rear lobed drive-flange feature if editable history exists. Otherwise remove the flower-profile lobe and scallop faces and trim the affected flange back to its adjacent planar shoulder, leaving the internal spline bore, front annular seating face, cylindrical pilot, rear circular boss, and all unaffected axial lands intact.

Extrude the master insert hexagon from interface_start_z through interface_depth and Boolean-union it with solid 0. Where necessary, limit the extrusion with the original flange start and end planes so the replacement has the same axial position and thickness as the removed flower interface. The six planar exterior faces must be parallel to the corresponding carrier-socket faces and centered on the spline axis.

Recreate the flange-to-shoulder transition at both ends of the hexagonal prism. Apply chamfers or small fillets matching the axial extent of the removed lobe transitions, but keep the central working portions of all six torque-reacting faces planar. Do not propagate these edge treatments into the internal spline faces, front cylindrical pilot, rear circular boss, or preserved annular seating faces.

operations_plan.summary: Reassemble the two solids and verify that the new hexagonal interface transfers torque without changing protected sprocket geometry.

steps.description: Return solids 0 and 1 to their original coaxial and axial assembly positions. Run an interference and minimum-clearance check over the full interface depth. Confirm that clearance exists between the male and female hex profiles, that the six pairs of working faces are parallel, and that corner radii and entry chamfers do not prevent insertion. Keep the insert as a separate solid unless the source assembly explicitly requires a bonded Boolean union.

Validate the preserved center geometry by comparing the final model with the original: internal spline tooth form, count, diameters, orientation, and axial extent must be unchanged; the rear circular boss and front pilot must retain their original diameter and axial location. Confirm that the new hexagonal faces do not break through the annular carrier or intersect any spoke root.

Validate all geometry outside the center interface against the original model. Preserve the curved radial ribs and apertures, outer support band, sprocket tooth count, pitch geometry, tooth flanks, overall thickness, and front and rear face contours. Regenerate the model and check for valid watertight solids, non-manifold edges, sliver faces, and unintended changes to the outer chain-engagement ring.
